label: Late original-phase n/x/u/i/h/g/2/v/e inputs and the <DEL> step, mainly when the sequence starts with p or a
explanation: Fires only in the original phase (from t>=3, and the rate climbs with position up to orig_idx 8) and on the <DEL> step. It never fires in the copy phase or at t<3. In the original phase it fires mostly on the first occurrence of one of the inputs n, x, u, i, h, g, 2, v, e (94% of activations are first occurrences). Firing depends heavily on the first token of the sequence: when it is p (8x lift) or a (7x), and to a lesser degree k, the rate is much higher, and the largest activations (on <DEL> and on late n/x/h/2 inputs) come almost entirely from sequences starting with p or a. It is rare on o, l and w inputs and on repeated tokens. The token-set-and-position condition alone covers 94% of activations but with only 6% precision. Adding first_tok in {p,a} raises precision to about 44% and F1 to about 0.45, keeping 58% of activation mass. The rest of the activations are spread over sequences with other first tokens, so this looks like a continuous hidden-state readout rather than a clean discrete feature.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: p, a, k, b, m, y; least: w, u, g, x) and the current input token (most: n, x, u, i, h, 2; least: y, p, j, a); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=7.
